title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1971-03-24
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Stunning soundboard capture of a high‑energy 3/24/71 Winterland set with a smoking Hard to Handle and tight band performance.
ai_review.review: The recording is a crisp, intimate soundboard mix that lets every instrument shine – the bass is thick, Jerry’s guitar tone cuts through, and the crowd ambience adds just the right amount of live atmosphere. Musically the show is a powerhouse: Hard to Handle erupts with blistering solos (Bob’s early solo and Jerry’s soaring lead), Phil drops bomb‑like bass lines, and the band rides high energy throughout, even if the source is incomplete. Overall listeners rave about the performance and consider it one of the finest early‑’71 outings.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating ≈4.86/5 across 21 reviews, with consistent praise for both performance and sound quality; only minor technical complaints (hiss, incomplete source) keep it from perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with intimate feel; occasional tape hiss and a few drop‑outs noted, but overall balanced sound. The source is incomplete (missing parts of the show).

show_quality.setlist_flow: High‑energy set with tight transitions; the band stays locked in from start to finish, though the recording cuts off before the final verses.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His solo on Hard to Handle is described as 'absolutely sick' and his 1971 guitar tone is praised for intensity and clarity; he 'cuts hard through the mix'.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass work is highlighted as thick, round, and bomb‑dropping power; multiple reviewers note his interplay with Jerry and a massive jam peak.
band_member_comments.Bob: First two solos on Hard to Handle are credited to Bob and praised for flow and inspiration; vocal rap on the song is called 'right on target'.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s absence noted as a plus, Billy’s drumming described as lean, tough and less cumbersome; overall drum work fuels the high energy.
